gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Denon DCD-600NE and Onkyo C-7030 both put out a fixed 2.0 V RMS analog line level (Onkyo rated into 600 Ω), so the stereo must offer a line-level CD/AUX/TAPE input and the player cannot drive volume itself, nor that the Denon caps data discs at 512 files/256 folders, 48–320 kbps MP3/WMA, refuses non-finalized CD-Rs and copy-protected WMA, and outputs digital on optical only.
standout_why: Compared against the pages ChatGPT got that I could open: insideouthomereviews.com (read 2026-11-08) already says the Denon is optical-only, that Yamaha's Pure Direct kills digital out and display, and that Denon has two Pure Direct modes; the Onkyo C-7030 manual (results 4-6) already carries the Onkyo 2.0 V/600 Ω and -22.5 dBm figures. Crutchfield compare pages, B&H compare, Sweetwater and the Yamaha specs page returned 403 so I could not confirm what they state; Crutchfield normally lists outputs but not output level or file limits. New here: Denon's 2.0 V RMS output level, its data-disc file limits and DRM/finalization refusals, and Onkyo's statement that digital out is 16-bit/44.1 kHz PCM and that RI needs an analog link regardless.
decides: For a stereo with a spare analog CD/AUX/TAPE input the mechanism does not separate the three: each delivers a fixed ~2.0 V RMS line level over RCA, so any of them works and the player has no volume control of its own (a PHONO input is the wrong place). The mechanism only decides the pick when the stereo's free input is digital: a coaxial-only input rules out the Denon DCD-600NE (optical only); any digital link needs Pure Direct off on the Yamaha CD-S303 or Mode 1 on the Denon, else silence. For shoppers with burned discs, the Denon manual says non-finalized CD-Rs and copy-protected WMA will not play and caps a data disc at 512 files and 320 kbps.
